query: other candidate methods for For the class-matched detections in one capture, select_stage2_subset ranks that DetectionCandidate list with the strategy select_detection already implements. It applies that strategy by the first-maximum rule std::max_element already uses, so a tie keeps the earlier candidate and the later tied candidate stays deferred. It admits at most the count the caller passes, in that rank order, and places every candidate it does not admit into deferred, preserving their order in the candidate list. Each candidate keeps its source_index. Stage2Admission holds those two vectors, admitted and deferred. An empty candidate list returns both vectors empty, and an unknown strategy throws. The pose node calls it with its detection_selection strategy and a count of one, so stage 2 still estimates that single admitted pallet. The admitted source index and the deferred source indices are written on PalletPoseStamped after input_depth_stamp. The message already carries this pair's RGB and depth stamps, so the split is this capture while the scene can still change. When the estimate fails, publish no PalletPoseStamped and write the same two lists on the failure diagnostic, which is the only result that path publishes. The two early returns that publish nothing stay as they are. The user named which detections are sent through stage 2 versus marked deferred. The part they did not name is that the split is these two admission vectors, ordered by that first-maximum rule, on the pose result the handling process reads. that are not the first list
findings: Soft-NMS rescores boxes that overlap the current maximum and keeps them in the same detection list. Bodla, Singh, Chellappa, and Davis sort by classification score, select the maximum M, and replace a hard zero with a penalty. The linear rule leaves the score unchanged when IoU(M, bi) is below Nt and multiplies by (1 - IoU) once IoU reaches Nt; the runs they report use Nt = 0.3. The Gaussian rule is si = si * exp(-IoU(M, bi)^2 / sigma) for every box not yet selected, and the runs they report use sigma = 0.5. The update repeats on the decayed scores, so a later box can become the next maximum. After each pass, boxes below 1e-4 are discarded. On COCO-style AP the Gaussian version lifts R-FCN from 31.1 to 32.4 and Faster R-CNN from 24.4 to 25.5 on MS-COCO test-dev. On PASCAL VOC 2007, Gaussian Soft-NMS moves Faster R-CNN from 37.7 to 39.4 and R-FCN from 49.8 to 51.4. Deformable R-FCN with multi-scale testing moves from 39.8% to 40.9%. Each pass is O(N) and the full procedure is O(N^2). The sort key is the classification score.

IoU-guided NMS ranks by predicted localization IoU. Jiang, Luo, Mao, Xiao, and Jiang set bm to the box with the largest predicted IoU, then delete every remaining box whose IoU with bm exceeds the NMS threshold. The classification score stored on bm becomes the maximum of its own score and the scores of the boxes it deleted. A lower classification score can be the box that stays, and the score written back is the cluster maximum. The paper reports that this procedure outperforms traditional NMS and Soft-NMS on MS-COCO. Deleted boxes leave the set.

DIoU-NMS starts from the highest classification score, then zeros a neighbor by center distance as well as overlap. Zheng, Wang, Liu, Li, Ye, and Ren keep si when IoU(M, Bi) - R_DIoU(M, Bi) is below epsilon, and set si to 0 when that quantity reaches epsilon. R_DIoU penalizes the distance between the two centers relative to the diagonal of the smallest enclosing box, so boxes with distant centers stay. On PASCAL VOC 2007, YOLOv3 trained with CIoU loss and evaluated with DIoU-NMS reports 49.32 AP, against 46.57 AP for the IoU-loss baseline (relative gain 5.91% AP). CIoU loss without DIoU-NMS is 49.21 AP. Zeroed boxes leave the ranked list.

Weighted Boxes Fusion replaces a cluster with one averaged rectangle. Solovyev, Wang, and Gabruseva sort boxes by decreasing confidence and group a box into a cluster when IoU exceeds THR; in their experiments THR = 0.55 was near the optimum. Cluster confidence is the average of member scores. Cluster coordinates are confidence-weighted averages. The fused score is then rescaled by min(T, N) / N, with T the cluster size and N the number of models. On an Open Images ensemble, mAP at IoU 0.5 is 0.5642 for NMS, 0.5616 for Soft-NMS, 0.5667 for non-maximum weighted, and 0.5982 for WBF. On one RetinaNet-ResNet152 with its last NMS removed (500 boxes), raw boxes score 0.1718 mAP, NMS at IoU 0.5 scores 0.4902, and WBF scores 0.4532. The authors measure WBF at about three times the runtime of standard NMS. The emitted rectangle is the weighted average of the cluster.

DETR assigns a fixed set of predictions with the Hungarian algorithm. Carion, Massa, Synnaeve, Usunier, Kirillov, and Zagoruyko decode N = 100 learned object queries in parallel and choose the permutation that minimizes the sum of pairwise costs. The cost for a non-empty target is the negative class probability plus a box term that mixes L1 and generalized IoU. A prediction with no match is the empty class, and the empty-class log-probability in the loss is down-weighted by a factor of 10. Inference drops non-maximum suppression. The output is the matched set of class-and-box predictions, including empty-class slots.

TOOD marks training anchors by a product of classification score and IoU. Feng, Zhong, Gao, Scott, and Huang set t = s^alpha * u^beta, adopt alpha = 1 and beta = 6, and for each instance treat the m anchors with the largest t as positives. They adopt m = 13; sweeping m over 5, 9, 13, 17, and 21 stays inside 42.0 to 42.5 AP on COCO minival. The remaining anchors are negatives in the loss. At inference the detector keeps boxes by non-maximum suppression on the aligned classification score. The full model reports 51.1 AP on MS-COCO at single-model single-scale testing, against ATSS 47.7, GFL 48.2, and PAA 49.0. The top-m split is the training assignment.

FoundationPose scores refined pose hypotheses and keeps the maximum. Wen, Yang, Kautz, and Birchfield embed each hypothesis against the cropped RGB-D observation as a 512-d vector, run multi-head self-attention across the K embeddings with no position encoding, and project the attended features to scores. The selected pose is the highest of those scores. A 2026 pallet-bin pipeline feeds RF-DETR-S boxes into that ranker and keeps the highest-scoring refined hypothesis. On 284 real RGB-D frames, pose accuracy stays stable when at least 25% of the bin is visible, and depth stays reliable from 2 m to 7 m. The ranked items are pose hypotheses of a detected bin.
